correctness.rationale: Verified the publisher's equations (2.1), (3.7), (3.9), (3.13), §4.2 and Table 3. The apparent permutation of the age and time arguments of I in the printed Q equation is a notational discrepancy and does not affect spatial decoupling. Outside the common compact seed set the pointwise disease-free solution has Q=I=0 and S time-constant; local uniqueness proves the support claim. For the constant background in (3.7), set u=cλ and A=η(1−γ)S₀. The integral M(u) of the tilted nonnegative exit density is positive and at most one. It is differentiable for u>0, with M′≤0 since a exp(−ua) is bounded locally in u>0, so F′(u)=A[M′(u)/(q+u)−M(u)/(q+u)²]<0. For any c>0, choosing u>A and λ=u/c gives F(u)<1, hence infimum zero in (3.13), not necessarily attained at zero. The positive-c derivative cF′(cλ) excludes the stationarity equation even when the level-one equation has a positive temporal root. The exact constant-hazard witness gives F(0)=4, F(1)=1, F(2)=4/9 and a strictly negative λ derivative. The published 0.23–3.5 km/week values do not follow from the printed definition. In contrast to the compact-support theorem, (4.3) seeds Q₀(x)=3exp(−|x|) everywhere at finite x; moving contours are not evidence of new spatial support. Read the frozen verification narrative and witness code without running the supplied script; one self-equality in the code is tautological, so spatial independence was checked from the actual equations instead.

The lack of coupling alone establishes support invariance, but the separate monotonicity and infimum calculations are needed to diagnose the precise inconsistency.

value.rationale: This matters as a correction to a definite published claim: it invalidates the positive numerical speed interpretation under the actual printed equations and explains why the displayed root conditions fail. It separates temporal growth, propagation into unseeded locations and contour motion under a positive tail, three quantities that would otherwise be conflated. It makes no claim about extending or improving the epidemic model.
